claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2024-07-26 reports: Beryl brought Category 3–4 winds to the Southern Grenadines; building damage was extreme on Union Island, extremely severe on Mayreau, severe on Canouan and much lower on Bequia and Mustique.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2024-07-26 reports: On Union Island, Beryl damaged the hospital, water network, power plant, airport and nearly all berthing structures; on Palm Island it damaged a desalination plant, while Mayreau suffered major structural and communications damage.

claim_decisions.reason: Retain bounded source-supported finding with vintage and causal limitations; no extrapolation to 2026 or evaluated impact.
claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2024-07-26 reports: The assessment estimated US$230.6 million in direct physical damage, about 22% of 2023 GDP; the Southern Grenadines accounted for US$186.8 million, or 81% of the national total.
claim_decisions.uncertainty: Rapid modeled reconstruction-cost estimate of direct physical damage, not economic output loss, households affected or measured recovery progress.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2019-08-02 reports: The policy describes small farms on slopes often above 30 degrees and reports that cultivation practices on these slopes contribute to landslides during heavy rain; local farmers also noted longer dry periods and more intense rainfall.

claim_decisions.statement: Source dated 2019-08-02 reports: The policy sets adaptation priorities for vulnerable populations and proposes stronger participatory planning, climate information and monitoring, and Grenadines microgrids using solar, wind and battery storage.

gaps: No climate–violence pathway is inferred from hazard exposure or recovery gaps; local infrastructure and capacity evidence stands on its own.

executive_assessment.text: Beryl impacts differed sharply among Union Island, Mayreau, Canouan, Bequia and Mustique, with named water, health and transport damage.
Five named schools and Union Island/Mayreau training add concrete recovery inputs; policy proposals and fabrication applications remain plans or reported outputs.
